content:
- Ran the required Ralph task switch, which removed `.ralph/current_task.txt` and updated the current/done task summaries plus task history.
- The remaining worktree is the expected task payload: code, docs, Docker configs, evidence, bug tasks, and Ralph bookkeeping.
- Next I am staging everything, reviewing the staged diff summary, then committing with the required task-finished message that includes validation evidence and the tracked switchover challenges.

- Started choose-task turn.
- Loaded list-active-tasks skill and found no previous progress entry for Choose-Task.
- Next: refresh Ralph summary and read current task state plus chooser rules.

- Refreshed current task summary and chooser rules.
- Found exactly two active candidates: both are unblocked bug tasks with <passes>false</passes> and <priority>high</priority>.
- Next: inspect the two bug task files and switchover-related code to choose the better first fix instead of defaulting to list order.

- Compared the two active unblocked high-priority bug tasks against the current switchover code path.
- Chose `.ralph/tasks/bugs/generic-switchover-request-can-stall-without-primary.md` because it is the broader and more severe bug: it can strand the shipped Docker cluster without an authoritative primary and requires manual clear, while the stale-seed bug is narrower and has a manual config workaround.
- Wrote that path to `.ralph/current_task.txt`. Next: quit immediately so the selected task can be executed.

- Read prior progress and .ralph/current_task.txt; active task is .ralph/tasks/bugs/generic-switchover-request-can-stall-without-primary.md.
- Read the bug task file; it is not started and has no execution plan yet, so this turn should be a design/plan pass, not implementation.
- Next I am inspecting the switchover code paths and using the improve-code-boundaries skill to produce a concrete TO BE VERIFIED -> NOW EXECUTE plan in the task file.

- Confirmed the switchover bug is a type/boundary issue: the same enum was being reused for operator input, persisted DCS state, and HA lifecycle decisions, with no origin metadata for the request.
- Per the TO-BE-VERIFIED workflow, I changed the core ADTs first: introduced `SwitchoverTarget`, introduced persisted `SwitchoverRequest { requested_from: LeaseEpoch, target }`, changed `SwitchoverState` to `None | Pending(SwitchoverRequest)`, rewired the API controller to stamp the current primary epoch into the persisted request, and collapsed the DCS command surface to one `PublishSwitchover(SwitchoverRequest)` path.
- Updated the active bug task file to `in_progress`, added the concrete execution plan, and ended it with `NOW EXECUTE`.
- I did not run `make check` / `make lint` / `make test` / `make test-long` in this turn because the user workflow says to quit immediately after the design/type rewrite and hand off the compile/test fallout to the execution pass.
- Next turn should propagate the new ADT through DCS snapshot rendering, HA decide/reconcile, CLI/status output, tests/docs, then use Red-Green TDD to prove: (1) targeted switchovers self-clear after takeover and (2) generic switchovers do not trigger a second demotion on the successor leader.

- Read previous Ralph progress and current task pointer.
- Confirmed the active task file is .ralph/tasks/bugs/generic-switchover-request-can-stall-without-primary.md.
- Next I am reading the task body to confirm whether this is an execution pass and to align the remaining code/test work with the task checklist.

- Read the active bug task and confirmed the plan is in NOW EXECUTE mode.
- Ran cargo check to expose the exact fallout from the new switchover ADT split.
- The only compile breaks are the expected old-variant references in src/ha/decide.rs and src/command/mod.rs; next I am replacing those with request-aware helpers so the red-green test loop can run on behavior instead of type errors.

- Propagated the new SwitchoverRequest/SwitchoverTarget shape through src/command/mod.rs and src/ha/decide.rs and restored cargo-check green without changing the old switchover behavior yet.
- Added the first tracer-bullet unit test in src/ha/decide.rs for the targeted case: once the requested replica is the new primary, HA should lead and clear the stale switchover request.
- Next I am running that single test red with cargo nextest, then I will make the minimal targeted-only HA change to turn it green before adding the generic regression test.

- The first targeted switchover tracer-bullet test is green after the minimal leader-branch fix: a successor leader targeted by the request now clears the request once the active epoch changes.
- I added the second tracer-bullet test for the generic case, but the first cargo nextest attempt failed in build setup with a missing rlib object file rather than a behavioral assertion.
- Next I am cleaning the package build artifacts and rerunning only that generic test to get the real red failure before generalizing the stale-request clearing logic.

- The Docker stack is up and healthy; node-a, node-b, and node-c all reached container health after building the compose image from the current code.
- My first manual status probe failed because I assumed the `pgtm` binary path was ./target/debug/pgtm, but this workspace is building into a different target layout.
- Next I am locating the real host binary path and then I will run the targeted and generic switchover walkthroughs against the live Docker cluster.

- Completed the red-green TDD loop for the switchover bug: added one failing HA decision test for targeted successor self-clear, made it green, then added one failing HA decision test for generic successor double-demote, and made that green by clearing any pending request whose requested_from epoch no longer matches the active leader epoch.
- Manually verified the fix against the shipped Docker stack using the host pgtm binary at target/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/debug/pgtm: targeted switchover from node-b to node-c settled healthy with no pending marker on any seed, then a generic switchover from node-c settled back on node-b with no pending marker and no manual clear.
- Updated the reference docs to describe the persisted SwitchoverRequest { requested_from, target } shape. Next I am running the required repo-wide gates: make check, make lint, make test, and make test-long.

- make check passed cleanly.
- make lint passed cleanly as a separate explicit run.
- make test is now in progress under cargo nextest; if it fails I will fix the first concrete failure and rerun before moving on to make test-long.

- make test passed cleanly under cargo nextest: 243 tests passed, 16 skipped, with 5 leaky tests reported by nextest but no failures.
- make test-long is now running the ultra-long HA profile.
- Next I will wait for make test-long to finish; if it passes, I can update the task file, switch Ralph tasks, commit, and push.

- make test-long passed setup and is currently running the long HA scenarios under the ultra-long nextest profile.
- I am intentionally not probing the Docker environment aggressively while those scenarios run, to avoid perturbing the test harness.
- Next I will wait for the suite to finish and then complete the Ralph/commit/push closeout if it is green.
